This short guide maps common steps in an existing NIS analysis to easyNIS.
The examples use invented discharges, including records from `nis_example()`
with illustrative diagnosis and procedure codes.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Match each code slot separately

A legacy scan that pastes slots together can match a code that never occurs
in any slot. This invented record splits `A123` across two diagnoses.

```{r split-slots}
split_slots <- data.frame(I10_DX1 = "A1", I10_DX2 = "234")
with(split_slots, grepl("A123", paste0(I10_DX1, I10_DX2)))
nis_flag_dx(split_slots, eligible = "A123")$eligible
```

For patterns such as `^A12.*|^B34.*`, use the prefixes `c("A12", "B34")`.
`nis_flag_dx()` checks each diagnosis slot on its own. `nis_flag_pr()`
does the same for procedure slots. Set `position = "principal"` to check
slot 1, `"secondary"` to check later diagnosis slots, or `"any"` to check
all available slots. Prefix arguments are normalized by removing periods
and spaces and converting to uppercase. Slot values are compared as stored.

The example starts from generated data and substitutes illustrative codes,
then creates diagnosis and procedure flags:

```{r prefixes}
example_path <- nis_example(years = 2018:2020)

nis_flagged <- nis_open(example_path, years = 2018:2020) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    I10_DX1 = dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 50, "A1234", "A12345"),
    I10_DX2 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "B341", "C005"),
    I10_PR1 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "0AB12", "0XY34")
  ) |>
  nis_flag_dx(cohort_dx = c("A12", "B34"), position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_dx(exposure = "B34", position = "any") |>
  nis_flag_pr(example_procedure = "0AB", position = "any")
```

Use a regex definition when the legacy rule constrains the rest of the code.
This example requires exactly two digits after `A12` in a diagnosis slot.
Both principal codes match the prefix, while only `A1234` matches the regex.

```{r suffix}
nis_flagged <- nis_flagged |>
  nis_flag_dx(eligible = list(regex = "A12[0-9]{2}"), position = "any")

nis_flagged |>
  dplyr::distinct(I10_DX1, cohort_dx, eligible) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Regex definitions match the whole stored slot, so outer `^` and `$` anchors
are optional. A legacy regex that intentionally matched only part of a code
needs an explicit pattern for the rest of the slot, such as a trailing
`.*` for an unconstrained suffix. Write case-sensitive patterns for the
stored uppercase, undotted NIS codes. The package passes regex patterns
through without the normalization applied to literal prefixes.

## Replace local recode helpers

If a local cleaning helper used `case_when()` to turn known HCUP codes such as
sex, payer, or discharge disposition into labels, remove those repeated
recodes. `nis_design()` calls `nis_label()` on the collected analysis data.
Known binary codes become logical, and multi-level codes become factors.
Both receive variable labels. You can call `nis_label()` directly on a
collected data frame when you need the same recoding outside `nis_design()`.

Keep custom study-derived variables in `mutate()`. Set their factor order
explicitly with `forcats::fct_relevel()`, and override the displayed label at
the table where it is used:

```{r design, eval=rlang::is_installed("forcats")}
study_design <- nis_flagged |>
  nis_design(
    cohort = cohort_dx & AGE >= 50,
    keep = c(
      AGE, FEMALE, DIED, LOS, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS,
      cohort_dx, exposure, example_procedure
    ),
    dollars = 2020
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_band = forcats::fct_relevel(
      factor(dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 65, "65 or older", "Under 65")),
      "Under 65"
    )
  )
```

Use `gtsummary` label overrides for derived variables; HCUP labels already
cover the common coded fields:

```{r table-labels, eval=rlang::is_installed(c("forcats", "gtsummary", "cardx", "survey", "gt"))}
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  study_design,
  by = exposure,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, age_band, DIED, LOS, cost_adj),
  label = list(
    FEMALE ~ "Female",
    age_band ~ "Illustrative age group",
    cost_adj ~ "Hospital cost in 2020 USD"
  )
)

table_one$table_body |>
  dplyr::select(variable, label) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
```

## Keep discharge disposition and mortality separate

Check source values alongside the derived outcomes and the displayed
disposition label before carrying over a legacy recode.

```{r outcome-codes}
outcomes <- nis_outcomes(data.frame(DIED = 1L, LOS = 2L, DISPUNIFORM = 6L))
outcomes[c("DIED", "DISPUNIFORM", "in_hospital_death", "discharge_disposition")]
as.character(nis_label(outcomes)$discharge_disposition)
```

This invented row has an in-hospital death flag and a disposition label of
“Home health care.” Check inconsistent pairs against the source-year coding
and keep a documented rule for handling them. Use `in_hospital_death` for
mortality and `discharge_disposition` for destination. See
[Hospitalization outcomes](outcomes.html).

## Declare the cohort with `nis_design()`

Older scripts may build `survey::svydesign()` with `HOSPID` and `TRENDWT`,
then call `subset()` for the analysis cohort. Those fields are not available
in current NIS releases. For the supported ICD-10 years, `nis_design()` uses
`HOSP_NIS`, `NIS_STRATUM`, and `DISCWT`, and makes hospital and stratum IDs
year-specific before combining years. Pass the cohort expression and the
columns to retain; do not filter to the cohort before constructing the
design.

The design retains one placeholder for each hospital-year with no cohort
discharges. This lets the survey domain retain the sampled hospital context
when estimating the declared cohort. The placeholder-row method is
experimental and should be validated against a full-data design for the
analysis at hand. After `nis_design()`, filters should only narrow the cohort
declared by its `cohort` argument.

## Replace charge adjustment and testing switches

If `adj_TOTCHG` was inflation-adjusted **charges**, its counterpart is
`charges_adj`. `cost_adj` estimates hospital **cost** by multiplying charges
by `CCR_NIS` before inflation adjustment. With `TOTCHG` and `CCR_NIS` in
`keep`, `nis_design(..., dollars = 2020)` creates both fields, as in the
example above. For a collected data frame, call `nis_cost(data, dollars =
2020)` directly.

Replace a `TESTING` switch that points to a small hand-picked data file with
`nis_example(years = 2018:2020)`. It writes an invented, temporary dataset
with the same broad column shape needed to run the pipeline; it contains no
study records.

The example directory can be removed after use with
`unlink(example_path, recursive = TRUE)`.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Regex expressions may encode suffix rules that a prefix flag cannot
>   reproduce. Review each code-set translation.
> - A pooled analysis needs year-scoped hospital and stratum identifiers and
>   a stated weight convention.
> - Never treat `nis_example()` results as study or national estimates.

[`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html),
[`nis_cost()`](../reference/nis_cost.html), and
[`nis_suppress()`](../reference/nis_suppress.html).
